messages:
kai: heads-up — FP8 enablement on H100/L40S is flapping in canary. Observed two classes of problems: ~10-20% throughput regression for short seqs and KV cache corruption on long-lived sessions. Rolling back fp8 on the hosted cluster for now.

cheng: saw similar on our staging stack. Was it the transformer-engine fp8 kernel update from last week?

marta: attaching quick profiler dump from h100-canary-4. This is the condensed sampler output (short seq, batch=4):
```
Top kernels by time:
  matmul_fp8_gemm      42.3%
  quantize_dequantize  18.7%
  attention_kv_permute 12.1%
  kv_read_write         9.4%
  memcopy               6.8%
```
Notice the quantize/dequantize step is non-trivial for seq<=64.

ryan: perf-bot reported p95 jump on h100 cluster: +14% after FP8 flip. Also L40S showed a small memory boundary write in one session (seen in logs as memcpy len mismatch).

julia: my hypothesis: kernel selection is toggling FP8 for micro-batches where the overhead of quantize/dequantize exceeds kernel speedup. If the runtime heuristics favor fp8 when they shouldn't, we lose.

cheng: confirmed — selection logic uses `enable_fp8: auto` and a fast path that only checks model-global throughput estimates, not sequence-length or kv reuse patterns. Patch in flight to add seq_len + kv_hotness checks. PR #4572.

marta: KV corruption root-cause (prelim): on L40S we reuse kv buffers across requests but skip zeroing when new kv size < previous allocation. FP8 kernels have different layout/stride and the allocator assumptions were wrong. Workaround: zero-init on reuse.

kai: for canary I forced transformer-engine flags:
```
--ft_fp8 TRUE 
--ft_fp8_mode E4M3 
--ft_fp8_autocast 0 
--cache-zero-on-reuse 1
--batch_heuristic max_batch_tokens=4096
```
This reduced the KV flakiness but throughput still worse for short seqs.

ryan: small note on calibration: static per-tensor calibration (one-shot) improved numeric quality vs dynamic, but it adds a pass that hurts latency. Dynamic per-iteration scaling is faster but had quality jitter on a subset of prompts.

julia: can we try hybrid: static calibration for key layers, dynamic for matmuls? That might reduce quantize overhead while keeping quality.

cheng: plan of attack: 1) add kernel-selection telemetry (emit why FP8 chosen: model, seq_len, batch_size, kv_reuse_flag), 2) change heuristic to prefer fp16 when (batch_size<8 || seq_len<32) or when kv_reuse_rate>0.7, 3) allocator: always zero-on-reuse for FP8 layouts, 4) nightly stability suite across H100 and L40S with long-session KV stress and short-seq throughput bench.

marta: running perf bench tonight against h100-canary-4 and l40s-canary-2. Acceptance: p95 <= +5% vs baseline and no KV mismatch logs for 24h. If either fails, we block auto-rollout.

kai: thanks. tagging @eng-sre for canary rollout orchestration and @perf-bot to keep watching. Post canary logs here, include `nvprof`/`nsys` traces and the kernel-selection telemetry. :eyes: 

infra-bot: deploy triggered: canary/h100/fp8-stability-2026-03-18 by kai

perf-bot: alert (automated): h100-canary-4 p95 increased 12% at 1775123530 — correlated with fp8 switch.

cheng: opened follow-up issues: 
- RD-891: kernel-selection telemetry and heuristic tweak
- RD-892: allocator zero-on-reuse for FP8
- RD-893: nightly fp8 stability job (H100 + L40S)

ryan: one more quick suggestion — when we choose FP8, try fusing quantize+matmul into a single kernel (if available) to avoid standalone quantize overhead. If transformer-engine has fused paths, prefer them for seq<=64.

marta: good call. I'll audit the kernel table and update mapping.

kai: if anyone reproduces KV corruption, capture a core dump + nvtx timeline and drop it here. We'll keep fp8 disabled on hosted until the stability job gives green.

cheng: working on PRs now, will post benchmarks and a small reproducible script in this thread when ready.

kai: solid. keep this thread as the single source-of-truth for the rollback + re-enable checklist. :thumbsup:
